definition: Partial insanity is a historical term for a supposedly limited form of mental disorder affecting only part of the mind, rather than a more general disturbance. In older psychiatry it was grouped under monomania, but that label later fell out of favor because such cases were seen as belonging to different clinical conditions, especially paranoid and other psychotic disorders.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Monomania; pinned source text

reasons: The packet does not explicitly state that “partial insanity” means “affecting only part of the mind”; it only links “partial insanity” to “monomania” and contrasts “more diffuse disorders,” without directly describing “only part of the mind.”

The definition claims the later disfavoring was because “such cases were seen as belonging to different clinical conditions, especially paranoid and other psychotic disorders.” The packet supports that writers abandoned “monomania” in favor of “PARANOIA” and critiques the term as reflecting an “uncritical attitude,” but it does not explicitly frame the reason in the exact way given (as “belonging to different clinical conditions”).
